subject: Urgent: FastFin observed latency/error surge against reserved pool - arranging stakeholder bridge
messages:
From: Elena Sokolova <elena@fastfin-pay.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: FastFin SRE <sre@fastfin-pay.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: production errors and latency spike against our reserved pool

Aditya —

We started seeing a marked increase in 5xx errors and tail latency for requests routed to our dedicated/reserved pool (customer_id=FF-8492) at ~07:40 PT. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to 4.8% and p99 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.9s. This affected several live flows (payment validation + anti-fraud scoring).

We’ve already throttled some downstream callers but the issue persists. Can you confirm whether this is a capacity saturation or an infra regression? We need an ETA for restoration and whether FastFin should expect failing transactions for the next hour.

Logs attached (fastfin_error_log_1201.txt). We are open to a bridge now.

—Elena
Elena Sokolova
Head of Platform Engineering, FastFin Payments

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Elena Sokolova <elena@fastfin-pay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: production errors and latency spike against our reserved pool

Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I’m escalating immediately.

Short answer: we believe this is reserved-capacity headroom exhaustion from a combination of a transient traffic spike and an autoscale lag in one of the pool shards. We are standing up a mitigation bridge now and looping in engineering and customers success.

Immediate steps I’ve kicked off:
- Ops: hot-bridge (joining now) to correlate redis/kvcache pressure and kernel-level qps per shard.
- Routing: temporary policy change to route a subset of FastFin traffic to compatible burst capacity while we stabilize the reserved pool (will maintain region and model parity).
- Throttles: recommending FastFin apply a light client-side backoff for non-critical flows for the next 20–30m.

I’ll update in the bridge; ETA for routing change push is ~8–12 minutes. If routing fails or load persists we will propagate to execs and propose an emergency credit for failed requests.

Aditya Rao
Head, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: production errors and latency spike against our reserved pool

Team — quick exec note for context (thread copied to me via FF SRE):

Summary: FastFin’s reserved pool (FF-8492) is experiencing sustained headroom pressure leading to elevated errors/latency on critical payment scoring routes. Customer is high-touch and at risk for revenue impact.

Asks for immediate attention:
1) Engineering (Neha + Rishi): confirm root cause hypothesis (autoscale lag vs kernel regression) and whether an emergency patch or config fallback can be applied to reduce p99.
2) Ops (Aditya): proceed with routing fallback and confirm the exact traffic % we can move to burst without violating contract.
3) Sales/Account (Marissa): prepare comms and a goodwill credit proposal if we exceed SLA impact thresholds.

Please update within the hour. If mitigation is not stable by 10:00 PT, I want a C-level notification prepared.

—Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: production errors and latency spike against our reserved pool

Update and interim RCA (attached draft PDF). Bridge notes:

Timeline summary:
- 07:38 PT: Observed p99 jump and 5xx spike for customer routes.
- 07:40–08:05 PT: Autoscaler failed to inject a spare shard due to an eviction storm on the shard controller (TTL recycle race).
- 07:52 PT: We pushed a temporary routing override (Aditya) — moved 18% of FastFin traffic to burst capacity; errors dropped to 0.6% and p99 returned to ~280ms.
- 09:10 PT: Controller restart fixed the eviction storm and autoscale resumed normal behavior.

Root cause (interim): a race in the shard controller during aggressive TTL-based eviction caused the controller to be slow to allocate spare capacity when the sudden spike hit. This exposed a scenario where reserved pool headroom collapsed transiently.

Mitigations completed:
- Hotfix queued for the controller to add a short, bounded allocation backoff to avoid the eviction storm (deploy scheduled 2026-12-03 02:00 UTC).
- Routing fallback formalized: we will permit cross-tier burst routing for FastFin for up to 25% traffic for 2 hours during similar events (documented in INF-1234).
- Postmortem doc and credit proposal drafted (attached).

Outstanding: need PR approval for controller backoff, and Marissa to finalize the goodwill credit recommendation. Vivek — please advise if we should proactively brief CEO/legal given contract exposure.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Serving Reliability — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
